thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: sustained tail latency on router->lb path in eu-central (p99 spike) detected by SLO-monitor at 12:03 UTC. Paging oncall maya. Auto-escalation to oncall group.

maya: I'm on it. grabbing perf graphs now. can someone paste the golden link?

ash: https://metrics.redwood/internal/dashboards/routers?range=1h&region=eu-central — p95 jumped to ~1.8s and p99 to ~6.5s starting at 11:58 UTC. streaming endpoints show stalls (clients timing out).

samira: seeing large spike in router outgoing queue -> LB backend 10.23.x.y. Hot partitioning on route-hash for model-qa-v2. Filtered logs show many 502->retry loops.

noah: Confirmed a config rollout 11:45 UTC pushed a new routing weight policy (feature flag: route-weight-v2). It changed affinity to prefer smaller shard pools to optimize cost; looks like it concentrated traffic.

maya: ok, hypothesis = policy rollout caused hot partition -> backend saturation -> tail latency/backpressure -> streaming stalls. impact: some customers on dedicated pools in eu are seeing >30% increase in tail errors. sales-jo, customer-ops, do we have an active customer hit list?

customer-ops: early notes: 3 paid customers reported elevated errors (alpha-saas, campusapp, docquery). alpha-saas has live demos active; we should notify them ASAP.

ops-bot: Runbook step 1: revert recent routing policy or reduce weight. Suggested quick mitigation: set route-weight-v2 = 0 (roll back).

maya: I'll roll back the flag to 0. Running: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/_flags/route-weight-v2 -d '{"value":0}'`

ash: Log tail while you do that. `kubectl logs -n router -l app=router --since=10m | grep 'hot-shard' -c` -> 124 matches.

maya: rollback command executed. flag is now 0. Confirming propagation...

noah: routing table push acknowledged by control plane. beginning gradual de-dup and rebalancing. Watching p99.

samira: immediate telemetry shows outgoing queue drain starting at 12:06 UTC. p99 dropped from 6.5s -> 2.1s in ~120s. streaming stall counts down by ~80% for affected streams.

maya: good. still seeing a few stragglers from overloaded backends; sending a rolling restart for the 10.23.* backend pool to clear connections: `pkill -HUP router-proxy` on relevant nodes.

ash: restarted proxies on 6 nodes. connection churn is healthy; no new 502 loops.

sales-jo: pinged alpha-saas and docquery with a status blurb: "we detected and rolled back a routing policy change causing elevated latency; mitigation in progress; we'll follow up with timeline and RCA".

customer-ops: customers acknowledged. alpha-saas temporarily disabled heavy streaming demos and saw error surface drop.

maya: summary for page: root cause = buggy rollout of route-weight-v2 that concentrated affinity into a small set of shards in eu-central causing hot partitions and backend saturation -> router queues/backpressure -> tail latency p99 spike and streaming stalls. Mitigation = rollback flag to 0 + rolling restart of affected proxies. Customer impact = elevated p95/p99 and increased error rates for a subset of eu customers between ~11:58-12:06 UTC.

noah: next steps: patch the flag rollout to include canary checks (detect hot-shard skew) and add an automated circuit-breaker that rejects rapid weight shifts > X% per minute. Also add a health probe to detect backend queue depth and automatically divert traffic to fallback variant.

samira: filing incident ticket #INC-2026 with logs, graph snapshots, and traffic heatmap. I'll attach the routing diff and flag rollout metadata.

maya: thanks. postmortem owners: samira (technical lead), noah (runtime mitigations), customer-ops (customer comms). We'll schedule a live RCA review tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem within 72 hours and tag severity-high.

maya: closing this thread for now. if anyone sees p99 creep again, re-alert and we'll re-open. :thumbsup:

ash: one-liner for timeline: 11:45 flag rollout -> 11:58 p99 rise detected -> 12:03 page -> 12:05 rollback -> 12:07 p99 trending down -> 12:15 streaming stalls largely recovered.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (automated): Latency SLO breach cleared. Logged as SEV2.
